title: EGP Graphai • Lexical Map Language Registry
description: Registry of a language's inflection categories and codes, letters, and key-normalization rules. One file per language, at lexical-maps/<language>/_language.json.

locale.description: Intl.Collator locale for display-time sorting, e.g. "el" for Greek or "he" for Hebrew and Aramaic. Not "grc" or "arc" — those are not collation locales and resolve silently to root collation.

sensitivity.description: Intl.Collator sensitivity. "accent" ignores case and sorts on accents, the setting the lexical map wants; "base" ignores accents too and is not wanted, since it ties distinct forms.

_id.description: Identifier for this key-normalization rule, e.g. "fold-grave".

description.description: Optional longer explanation of what the rule folds and why.

_id.description: Identifier for this category, e.g. "tense" or "voice". A parse may carry at most one code from any one category (checked outside this schema).

required.description: Whether a parse for the relevant part(s) of speech must carry a code from this category (checked outside this schema).

description.description: Optional longer explanation, e.g. why this category is kept apart from a related one.

_id.description: Code for this inflection value, e.g. "aor" or "midpas". This is the token a parse array carries, and it must resolve in a parse (checked outside this schema).

category.description: _id of the inflectionCategories entry this code belongs to.

description.description: Optional longer explanation, e.g. for a code minted to resolve a genuine ambiguity such as "midpas".

_id.description: Identifier for this kind of class, e.g. "declension" or "conjugation". A root carries at most one class per category, under a key of this name.

description.description: Optional longer explanation, e.g. why the citation form does not always reveal which class a word belongs to.

_id.description: Code for this class, e.g. "2m" or "contract-a". This is the value a root's own declension or conjugation carries, and it must resolve here (checked outside this schema).

category.description: _id of the classCategories entry this class belongs to.

appliesTo.description: Parts of speech a root may carry this class on. A declension class applies to nouns and adjectives, a conjugation class to verbs.

gender.description: The gender every noun in this class has, where the class has one. A root carrying this class and a different gender is a contradiction (checked outside this schema). Declined on purpose by the classes that hold more than one gender: "3-cons" covers all three, "3-syncopated" holds πατήρ beside μήτηρ, and "indeclinable" is not a paradigm.

description.description: Optional longer explanation of what distinguishes this class from a neighbouring one.

_id.description: Short identifier for the language, e.g. "greek". Names the lexical-maps/<language>/ directory.

script.description: Script this language is written in, matching the script codes in content-schema.json.

citationConvention.description: Prose describing how a root is cited, e.g. which principal part or grammatical form a lexicon headword names.

collation.description: Intl.Collator settings for display-time sorting of this language's forms. Files themselves sort by NFD code point, which is stable across ICU versions.

normalization.description: Ordered key-normalization rules applied when forming a codex key from an attested surface form.

letters.description: Ordered alphabet. Each entry names one codex file under lexical-maps/<language>/, and the order also drives display order.

inflectionCategories.description: Categories a parse code can belong to. A parse may carry at most one code per category (checked outside this schema).

inflections.description: Every code usable in a parse array, each tied to one category. Every code in a parse must resolve here (checked outside this schema).

style.description: Name of the scheme, such as `academic`.

description.description: What the scheme does and what it is for.

lossy.description: Features the scheme does not represent, so a reader knows where the round trip breaks.

letters.description: Base letter to its Latin rendering.

diphthongs.description: Two-letter sequences that read as one sound.

velars.description: Letters that turn a preceding gamma into a nasal.

gammaNasal.description: Rendering of gamma before a velar.

upsilonInDiphthong.description: Rendering of upsilon closing a diphthong.

transliteration.description: Table driving transliteration. Kept as data so a consumer can read it rather than reimplement the scheme.

classCategories.description: The kinds of lexical class a root can carry. Separate from inflectionCategories: a class is a fact about the headword and says which paradigm it follows, while an inflection category describes one form of it.

classes.description: Every class a root may name, across all categories. A root's own declension or conjugation must be one of these (checked outside this schema).

description.description: Optional explanation of what a reading is and why it is not the same thing as a part of speech.

readings.description: Part of speech to the others a word of that part of speech may legitimately be tagged with. A corpus records the reading a token has in its own sentence, which need not be the heading its lexicon files the word under: a noun used attributively reads as an adjective.

posReadings.description: Which cross-part-of-speech readings are allowed, so a cell whose parse names a different part of speech than its root is not automatically a defect.
